independence: Only the source paper raster was read. No WSPRadar outputs or implementation files were inspected. Source-only zooms and dark-pixel component centroids were used.
selection_rule: Scan chronologically, selecting the first eligible negative extreme, then the first eligible positive extreme after it, then the first eligible negative extreme after that. Eligibility requires the full +/-2 pixel vertical interval to lie below -10 dB or above +20 dB, at least 20 pixels to another identified black-dot centroid, and more than 10 pixels to colored contours and axes. This alternating-sign rule addresses the incompatibility between literal first-three selection and distinct signs: the literal first three extremes are all negative. No comparison with computed outputs informed selection.
selection_limit: The chronological rule takes precedence over the preference for wide coverage of the day. All three selected points occur before 08 UTC.
original_annotation_scope: The independence, selection_rule and selection_limit fields above describe the original three-point extraction. All three original witnesses and their coordinates remain unchanged; comparison_label selects the current displayed subset independently of regression coverage.

display_revision.selection_request: Keep displayed P1 and P2, move displayed P3 to the later source points at the -15 dB plot boundary, and add a clear later-day positive point as P4. Retain the former displayed P3 as an undisplayed regression witness.
display_revision.selection_basis: P3 is the right-hand one of the two visible black-dot caps at the lower plot boundary near 08-09 UTC. P4 is the isolated positive dot near 16 UTC and +24 dB. Both were selected from the original raster and their source pixel coordinates recorded before checking their correspondence with native pairs. Earlier reconstruction review had already occurred; this is retrospective source-guided annotation, not a blinded selection.
display_revision.clipped_point_method: The new P3 dot merges with the horizontal axis at raster rows 791-792. Its recorded centroid uses only its visible 9-pixel upper cap at rows 789-790, excluding the axis. This is not the centroid of a fully resolved dot; its calibrated ordinate is a visible-cap readout near -15 dB. No correction toward a native observation was applied.
display_revision.tolerance_policy: The existing 0.08-hour and 0.21-dB comparison tolerances are unchanged. The new P3 is an explicitly axis-clipped witness and does not satisfy the original isolated-dot clearance rule. P4 extends the displayed time coverage beyond the original chronological selection.

display_revision_history.supersedes: The P3 display selection recorded in display_revision; all earlier source witnesses remain in points for regression coverage.
display_revision_history.selection_request: Move displayed P3 to the complete source dot just above the previous lower-boundary witness, near 09 UTC and -14 dB. Keep P1, P2 and P4 unchanged.
display_revision_history.selection_basis: The requested source dot is the complete 18-pixel dark component with centroid (573.5, 771.222222), selected and calibrated from the original raster before checking its native-pair correspondence. This is a retrospective user-directed selection with prior familiarity with the reconstruction, not a blinded selection.
display_revision_history.display_change: isolated_negative_3 now carries P3. clipped_negative_1 retains its original coordinates, clipping caveat and regression check with comparison_label null.
display_revision_history.tolerance_policy: The existing 0.08-hour and 0.21-dB comparison tolerances and source calibration remain unchanged. No marker coordinate was adjusted toward a native observation.

centroid_method: Mean coordinates of the 8-connected dark-pixel component near the independently selected visual dot, with all RGB channels below 80. Decimal coordinates describe raster arithmetic, not physical measurement precision.

recommended_comparison_tolerance.reason: Conservatively includes annotation and approximate axis-calibration uncertainty. Declare this before comparing outputs.

points.interpretation: Visible upper cap of the right-hand lower-boundary dot near 08:30 UTC; the dot merges with the -15 dB axis. The source readout is preserved rather than moved to an exact native SNR value.
An isolated positive source dot near 16 UTC extends the displayed witnesses into the later part of the day without inferring its date or station identity from the paper.
Complete negative source dot near 08:45 UTC, above the lower plot boundary; selected for displayed P3 without changing the earlier witnesses or inferring its date or station identity from the paper.

interpretation_limit: These annotations test existence of a plotted UTC-hour and Delta-SNR combination within declared tolerances. The figure does not identify the date or complete station-path evidence for an individual point. Agreement cannot establish complete identity, pairing provenance, or correctness of the full distribution.
